cues.text: In 480 BC, a few thousand Greeks blocked the road into Greece.
Marching south: the army of Persia, the largest empire of its time.
They chose a pass called Thermopylae. The Hot Gates.
Mountains on one side. The sea on the other.
At its narrowest, says Herodotus, room for just one cart.
About 7,000 Greeks, with 300 Spartans, held it for two days.
Then a local man showed the Persians a path over the mountain.
It came down behind the Greeks.
For 25 centuries, rivers have carried silt into the gulf.
The sea is now kilometres away.
The narrow road where the Spartans fell is gone.
